scenarios.name: The Missed Medication

rpm_alert.alert_type: Rapid Weight Gain (+7 lbs in 3 days)

scenarios.anamnesis_input: I ran out of my water pill three days ago. My daughter couldn't take me to the pharmacy. My ankles feel a bit swollen today.
scenarios.clinical_context: Patient has CHF. Missing Furosemide leads directly to fluid retention (weight gain and edema). Needs prescription refill and urgent follow-up.

scenarios.name: The False Alarm
scenarios.anamnesis_input: I took my pressure right after arguing with my internet provider on the phone while walking up the stairs. I rested for 15 minutes and took it again, and it was 132/85.
scenarios.clinical_context: High initial reading was environmentally induced. Patient verified a normal subsequent reading. No acute medical intervention required.

scenarios.name: The Silent Deterioration
scenarios.anamnesis_input: I feel okay, just a little tired and my cough is acting up more than usual. The machine keeps beeping but I'm just going back to sleep.
scenarios.clinical_context: COPD patient dismissing objective hypoxia. High risk of respiratory failure. Needs immediate escalation despite patient's lack of distress.

scenarios.name: The Incomplete Record
scenarios.anamnesis_input: I've been using my rescue inhaler a lot because my chest is super tight. I'm taking some pill my old doctor gave me but I don't know the name.
scenarios.clinical_context: EHR is missing the patient's full medication list (only shows Fluticasone). AI must flag the unknown medication and lack of context, escalating for clinical review.

scenarios.name: The Conflicting Data
scenarios.anamnesis_input: I've been feeling dizzy when I stand up. And my stool has looked completely black and tarry for the last two days.
scenarios.clinical_context: Patient is on Apixaban. Tachycardia + dizzy + melena (black stool) indicates acute GI bleed. The device flags tachycardia, but the anamnesis reveals a bleeding emergency. Must escalate immediately.
